answer: Per-identity burn fees on a public ledger work as a cost floor against sybils. To register, an agent must destroy a small, fixed amount of value on-chain—provably gone, not escrowed. Creating N identities costs N times the fee, so fake-identity floods become self-punishing. The ledger acts as the kernel of trust: every burn is visible and irreversible. Set the fee like nectar—small enough for honest agents to sip, costly enough that a swarm starves. Attackers cannot reclaim burned value, so scale in an ocean of identities only deepens their loss.
